lessons.title: Teams Direct Routing signaling
lessons.summary: Direct Routing uses the pstnhub proxies on 5061, a certified SBC, and a verified domain. Contact must be an FQDN.
objectives: Name the three signaling FQDNs and port 5061
Require a verified domain and an FQDN Contact
Remember that connection aliasing is unsupported

illustration.title: Direct Routing signaling
illustration.caption: Checked against the plan and protocol articles.
rows: Not supported by the SIP proxy

paragraphs: Direct Routing signaling uses sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com, sip2.pstnhub.microsoft.com, and sip3.pstnhub.microsoft.com on port 5061. TLS 1.2 or later is required, and the SBC is a certified SBC.
The synthetic INVITE targets sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com:5061 from sbc1.example.com. The real routing among the three proxies is in the plan and protocol articles.
The Contact must be an FQDN. If Contact is an IP address the proxy returns 403. The domain on the trunk must be a verified tenant domain, not a name ending in onmicrosoft.com.
The protocols article says the SIP proxy does not support RFC 5923 connection aliasing. Microsoft says wildcard names in the certificate CN or SAN are supported for Direct Routing.

lessons.title: OPTIONS health and SRTP media
lessons.summary: OPTIONS followed by 200 marks the SBC healthy. Media processors use SRTP. The protocol article’s OPTIONS CSeq cell disagrees with RFC 3261.
objectives: Mark health with OPTIONS and 200
Keep CSeq method equal to OPTIONS
Treat media-processor audio as SRTP

illustration.title: Health, then media
illustration.caption: Confirm CSeq with a capture. The table cell checked on 2026-10-14 is not the RFC.

paragraphs: Direct Routing uses OPTIONS, and a 200 OK marks the SBC healthy. The lab request is OPTIONS sip:sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com:5061 with CSeq: 1 OPTIONS and Contact sip:sbc@sbc1.example.com.

The SIP protocol article’s OPTIONS example table, checked on 2026-10-14, lists CSeq: 1 INVITE. That cell conflicts with RFC 3261, which requires the CSeq method to match OPTIONS. Teach the RFC, and confirm with a capture rather than copying that table cell.
Media processors use SRTP. The synthetic offer uses RTP/SAVP and c=203.0.113.20 so the profile on the wire is SRTP, as RFC 3711 names it.

This lesson does not invent a media-bypass prerequisite list. If you need the media path for a specific tenant, capture the RTP profile and read the current media article instead of guessing from signaling alone.

lessons.title: Webex Calling Local Gateway
lessons.summary: An IOS XE Local Gateway uses SIP TLS and SRTP. Third-party SBCs use a certificate-based trunk. Wildcard certificates are not supported. ByoPSTN means bring your own PSTN.
objectives: State the IOS XE TLS and SRTP requirement
Use a certificate-based trunk for a third-party SBC
Define ByoPSTN from the get-started article

illustration.caption: 192.0.2.40 stands for the Webex peer. Real names are in the IOS XE article.

sections.h: What the IOS XE article requires
paragraphs: The IOS XE local gateway article uses SIP TLS toward Webex and SRTP for media. The synthetic INVITE is TLS from 203.0.113.20, Contact sip:sbc@sbc1.example.com, and the offer is RTP/SAVP.
192.0.2.40 is only the lab stand-in for the Webex signaling peer. Take the real peer names from that article rather than from this page.
The trunks article says a third-party SBC is supported as a Local Gateway with a certificate-based trunk. The get-started article says wildcard certificates are not supported for Local Gateway.
ByoPSTN means bring your own PSTN in the preferred-architecture terminology cited from the get-started article. It is the premises path, and it is a different choice from Cloud Connected PSTN.

lessons.title: Three PSTN choices, one per location
lessons.summary: Webex Calling offers Cisco Calling Plan, Cloud Connected PSTN, or premises-based PSTN through a Local Gateway. A location has one PSTN connection.
objectives: Name the three PSTN choices
Give a location one connection
Keep Cloud Connected PSTN distinct from Local Gateway

illustration.title: PSTN choices
illustration.caption: Configure the location in the organization PSTN article.
rows: A cloud PSTN partner through Webex

paragraphs: The organization article lists Cisco Calling Plan, Cloud Connected PSTN, and premises-based PSTN through a Local Gateway. A location has one PSTN connection.

The ladder in this lesson is only the premises path: the Local Gateway at 203.0.113.20 sends the call to the carrier stand-in 192.0.2.40. That is ByoPSTN in the get-started article’s preferred-architecture language.

sections.h: Do not merge the cloud partner with the gateway
paragraphs: Cloud Connected PSTN is a cloud PSTN partner connected through Webex. It is not your SBC, and it is not the Local Gateway trunk.
Choosing both for one location fights the one-connection rule. Pick the choice in the organization article, then follow the Local Gateway articles only when the choice is premises-based PSTN.

sections.h: SIPREC is not a call-control trunk
paragraphs: An external voice system can send SIPREC into a conversational analytics connector. RFC 7866 is the recording protocol and RFC 7865 is the metadata. In this synthetic, 203.0.113.20 sends the session toward 198.51.100.30, which stands for the connector.

The ladder uses one SDP so the lab stays on addresses we can show. A production SIPREC body is the multipart body in those RFCs and in the connector document. Chime SDK Voice Connector is a SIP trunking service. Bridging an external carrier into Connect through Voice Connector is not a supported pattern unless an AWS specialist reviews and approves it.

lessons.title: Five9 BYO SIP and Twilio trunks
lessons.summary: Five9 BYO SIP connects your ITSP or gateway to Five9 SBCs. Twilio termination and origination are different directions, with a strict Request-URI rule.
objectives: Define Five9 BYO SIP and the gateway option
Separate Twilio termination from origination
Keep origination URLs on the sip scheme

illustration.title: Twilio directions
illustration.caption: Five9 is a different provider with its own BYO SIP document.
rows: Termination URI, plus IP ACL and/or credentials
sip scheme. sips is not supported
Your ITSP or gateway connects to Five9 SBCs

paragraphs: BYO SIP means the customer ITSP or gateway connects to Five9 SBCs. A gateway-to-gateway option is documented, and self-service exists for entitled BYO SIP trunk groups.

This lesson states no country limitation. In the synthetic, 203.0.113.20 is the customer gateway and 192.0.2.40 stands for a Five9 SBC. Use the BYO SIP document for the real peer addresses on an entitled trunk group.

Termination is your infrastructure toward the PSTN. It requires a termination URI plus an IP ACL and/or credentials. If the Request-URI does not reference the termination URI, Twilio treats the request as malicious and drops it.

Origination is PSTN calls toward your PBX via an origination SIP URI. The origination SIP URL schema is sip. The API reference says sips is not supported on origination URLs. In this lab the termination URI host is sbc1.example.com.

lessons.title: Genesys BYOC and NICE CXone SIP
lessons.summary: BYOC Cloud and BYOC Premises can be combined. NICE CXone documents SIP trunks on 5060 and 5061 with dynamic RTP and SRTP. Confirm carrier details with NICE.
objectives: Separate BYOC Cloud from BYOC Premises
Keep the hardware date on the Genesys Hardware Solution
State CXone ports without inventing a BYOC menu

illustration.title: Two vendors, documented scopes
illustration.caption: December 1, 2026 applies to the Genesys Hardware Solution.
rows: SIP over the public internet to the Genesys media tier
RTP crosses the internet. Far end needs a public address
Cloud and Premises can be combined
SIP trunks, ports 5060 and 5061, dynamic RTP/SRTP

paragraphs: BYOC Cloud is SIP over the public internet to the Genesys media tier. RTP crosses the internet, and the far end needs a public address. In this synthetic those roles are 203.0.113.20 and 192.0.2.40.

BYOC Premises is a customer-managed Edge. The two can be combined with hybrid media. The BYOC Premises article says Genesys Hardware Solution support ends December 1, 2026. That date is not a date for Customer Hardware.

sections.h: NICE CXone, only what those two pages say
paragraphs: The CXone connectivity and port documents describe SIP trunks, ports 5060 and 5061, and dynamic RTP and SRTP. This lesson does not invent a BYOC menu.
Account-specific carrier connectivity must be confirmed with NICE. Do not copy a Genesys public-address rule or a port range from another vendor into a CXone design.
